I want you to know that Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius"</note> is not correctly mixed, nor perfectly, with bodies; for a Spirit cannot be perfectly mixed with bodies unless they have been reduced into the appearance of nature. And therefore, when you wish to mix Mercury, or common Gold <note>original: "Sol"</note> or Silver <note>original: "Luna"</note>, those bodies must be reduced into the *appearance of Nature*, which is called common quicksilver <note>original: "argentum vivum vulgare"</note> through the bond of natural love, and then the male is joined to the female. Because our quicksilver is hot and dry in its action, while common quicksilver is cold and moist in its passive state, like a female who is contained in her dwellings with temperate heat until the eclipse <note>In alchemy, an "eclipse" refers to the *nigredo* or blackening stage, where the metallic "bodies" seem to die or disappear into a dark mass.</note>. And they are made black, like coals, which is the secret of our true dissolution; and from this, they are at last truly connected among themselves, so that they are never separated from one another. They become a very white powder; these are the Male and Female, generated by the bond of true love. These Children, however, will multiply their species into infinity, for *from one ounce* of this powder you will make infinite parts, and you will reduce it into Silver <note>original: "Luna"</note> better than any metal taken from a mine.

### On the Multiplication of Our Quicksilver.

Take <note>original: "REC." for "Recipe"</note> three *grossi* <term>Grossi: A unit of weight used by apothecaries and alchemists, roughly equivalent to a dram or 1/8 of an ounce</term> of pure Silver, in thin sheets, and make an amalgam with 4 *grossi* of well-washed common quicksilver. And when the amalgam has been made, then let it be placed in a small vessel <note>original: "metreto"; a glass jar or measure</note> with a neck one and a half feet long. Then take our quicksilver previously extracted and reserved *from the lunar body* <note>The "lunar body" refers to the Silver used in the previous step of the process</note>, and let it be placed over the amalgam made of the [silver] body *and the common quicksilver*. Let the vessel be sealed very well with lute <term>Lute: A clay or cement used to hermetically seal alchemical vessels to prevent the escape of vapors</term>, and let it be allowed to dry. This being done, let the vessel be moved as well as possible, so that the amalgam can be thoroughly mixed, and that the [our] quicksilver may be mixed with the body. Then place your vessel, in which the matter is, into a furnace at a small charcoal fire, and the heat of this fire should not exceed the heat of the Sun when it is in the Sign of Leo <note>This refers to the peak heat of summer; the alchemist is cautioned to use a gentle, natural heat rather than a violent one</note>. Because any other exceeding heat would destroy your matter, and a flight of one from the other would occur <note>The "flight" refers to the volatile spirits evaporating away from the fixed base</note>. Continue such a fire until the matter has become black like coals, and thick like porridge, and let the fire of this degree be continued until the matter changes into a dark gray color; and when the gray appears, then at that point let the fire be increased to the 2nd degree, until the matter begins to be whitened to the color of the whitest snow. Afterward, let the fire be increased to the 3rd degree, continuing until the matter is whiter than snow, and it is converted into pure powders whiter than ash. And then you have the living lime <term>Calx: A powder or friable substance produced by roasting a metal or mineral; the "Living Lime" is the perfected state of the matter</term> of the Philosophers, and THEIR SULPHUROUS ORE, which the Philosophers have hidden so much.

### The Property of the Aforesaid Lime.

This Lime converts common Mercury into a very white powder INTO INFINITY, which can be reduced into true silver with some body like Silver.

## Multiplication of this *Aforesaid Lime*.

TAKE <note>original: "REC." for "Recipe"</note> the vessel with the Matter, where you will place two ounces of common quicksilver <note>original: "argenti vivi vulgi"</note>, well washed and dried. Afterward, with the vessel well sealed with clay <note>original: "lutato," referring to 'lute,' a paste used to airtight-seal alchemical apparatus</note>, put it back where it was before, governing and administering to it the fire of the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd degrees, as described above, until the matter is reduced into a very white powder; and in this way, it can be multiplied into infinity.

## Reduction of *Quicklime* into *True Silver*.

Having therefore obtained a great quantity of *Quicklime* <note>original: "Calvis vivæ," likely a typo for "Calcis vivæ"</note>, or *OUR MINERAL*, take a vessel, or a Crucible, uncovered, in which you place one ounce of pure Silver <note>original: "Lunæ"</note>. Once it is melted, place four ounces of your powder over it in the form of pills—the pills should weigh a quarter of an ounce each. These are to be placed one after another upon the melted Silver, always continuing a strong fire, until all the pills have been cast in and melted together with the Silver. At the end, make a strong fire until the whole is well incorporated; afterward, let it be poured into a casting mold <note>original: "canali"</note>, and you will have 5 ounces of pure silver, more excellent than the natural kind. In this way, you will be able to multiply your *PHYSICAL MINERAL* at your pleasure. Thus far speaks *Lullius* <note>referring to Ramon Llull, a 13th-century philosopher to whom many alchemical works were attributed</note>.

See the rest in the *Clavicula* <note>The "Little Key," a common title for instructional alchemical manuals</note>, but since *Lullius* makes mention of a certain *Stinking Solvent* <note>original: "Menstrui Fætentis"</note>, the investigation of which would surely require another—and indeed a *Cabalistic Key of Solomon*—it is obvious to anyone who does not wish to be deceived that this *Stinking Solvent* is not to be understood literally. However, so that the true genealogy of this *Solvent* may appear, it would be necessary to survey those *Four Great Admirable Solvents* in the Philosophical World. Yet all are comprised within the *Circle of Mercury*. 

For in the *first preparation* (to use the terms of *Basil Valentine* <note>A legendary 15th-century alchemist, supposedly a Benedictine monk</note>), a greater, more perfect, and thinner Leaf, or golden opacity—namely *Physical Gold*—is introduced into Mercury, and then it is called the *Mercury of the Philosophers*, which afterward perfects itself without any other substance or thing, not only into Gold, but into a tincture. (Here Mercury behaves as a Male, newly coupled.) 

In the *second preparation*, its *Metallic* leaf is extracted from the Mercury (which is called the "spoils") so that the Mercury becomes a *Transparent* <note>original: "Diaphanus"</note> liquor. Because it can find that which it lost in no body except its own equal, it does not return to its former condition; instead, because of its weight and its ability to penetrate without reacting back, it dissolves and separates the bodies with which it is mixed according to their quantity. This is the true and unique essential solution, for bodies and the parts of bodies differ specifically from one another only as much as their quantities differ. This liquor is called *Alkahest* <note>A mythical universal solvent capable of dissolving every other substance</note>. (Here Mercury behaves as a widow.) 

In the *third preparation*, Mercury is taken before it has acquired any "leaf"—namely, before it has been specified—and then it is the **VIRGIN LIQUOR, SHINING**, and yet not burning. (Here Mercury behaves as an undefiled Virgin.) 

In the *fourth preparation*, the *Stinking* solvent of our mercurial harlot is taken, she who has played the prostitute with many and suffered the reaction, but yet has never conceived; instead, she infects everything she touches with the mercurial disease. And so, in truth, the **LIQUOR**

WHICH IS MERCURIAL, and yet not Virgin, and yet not *Mineral*, but MERCENARY <note>original: "meretricius," literally "prostitute-like." In alchemy, this refers to a "mercenary" mercury that acts as a medium or solvent but does not belong to the "pure" categories of virgin or fixed mineral.</note>, or a middle state between both. (Here *Mercury* behaves like a *prostitute*; who nevertheless never conceived.) It would be much labor to explain this liquid, for the entire scale of combinations is needed to find it. Therefore, more about these elsewhere, perhaps in my *Mercurial Concordance*. Meanwhile, learn from what has been said that two things are to be observed in Mercury. First, regarding its Decomposition, and insofar as it is a mixture; for in that State it admits either a greater Decomposition, which is essential, as in the *Mercury of the Philosophers*, or a superficial one, as we see in *Cinnabar* <term>Cinnabar: a bright red mineral consisting of mercury sulfide, the most common ore of mercury</term>, and Sublimate: or it admits a Resolution of the decomposed state, whether essential, as with the *Alcahest* liquor <term>Alcahest: a hypothetical "universal solvent" capable of reducing any body to its first matter</term>, or accidental, as in *mercurial Oils*. Second, regarding its Simple State *without composition*, where either *Mercury* has experienced no mineral leaf <note>original: "folium minerale," likely referring to the thin layers or "flakes" found in ores</note> at all, and then that wonderful, gleaming, and shining *Saline Virgin Sulfur* <note>original: "Sulphur Salinum Virgineum," a theoretical pure substance thought to be the seed of minerals</note> exists, and it acts only by *irradiating Metals*. Next, when *Mercury* has indeed experienced no metallic leaf, but nevertheless in its prior virgin form has undergone not a Decomposition, but a reaction with other things—*yet not Mineral ones*—hence now acting apart from reaction, it is most closely disposed toward *mercurification*. By the same reasoning through which the *Arsenical Sulfur of Sea Salt* is made in Mines, and by the light touch of a certain *Mineral* deviates into a Decomposed state of Quicksilver; you have the genealogy of *Lullius’s Stinking Menstruum* <term>Menstruum foetens Lulliani: a powerful, pungent solvent described in the works of Ramon Llull</term> and the *Paracelsian Circulate* <term>Circulati Paracelsici: a liquid purified and empowered by circular distillation</term>. But now time commands that we not be overwhelmed by the variety and weight of things to be said, and that we depart from the *Sixth Ore*, upon which we have dwelled long enough (though we would more gladly linger here than in the following rigid *Seventh Ore of Mars* <note>The "Seventh Ore of Mars" refers to iron or the chemical processes associated with it</note>.) And although we depart, that noble and penetrating sound still remains and wanders in our ears, which we perceived in this *Sixth Ore* from the MOST ANCIENT GOLDEN CYMBAL (A Manuscript; see volume *Three of the Chemical Theater*, page 781), of this tenor:

> *There exists only one thing of our Art, to which nothing foreign is added from beginning to end that is alien to its nature; and it is the nature of the purest quicksilver, for from a smoky resolution both in the bowels of the earth and in the Philosophical vessel, an unctuous vapor is generated, from which, through the action of Heat, at the end of digestion, a perfect metal is generated, from which further, through the resolution of Art aiding Nature, the Philosophical Stone is generated. So that there may be a shortcut in the Art: join the digested—indeed the most digested—metal to the crude, so that the mature may assist the immature, and element may be excited by element.*

Unless God had made this Ore, our study would be in vain. In what, however, the nature of such purest quicksilver consists, and its smoky resolution: *Geber, third part, book 1, chapter 27* <note>Geber is the Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, the foundational figure of Islamic alchemy</note> points it out when he writes: *And this is the method: that first each of them (namely, quicksilver and sulfur) is converted to an earthy nature, and from both of these earthy natures a most thin smoke is resolved by the multiplied heat in the Bowels of the earth; and this double smoke is the immediate matter of metals. When this smoke has been cooked by the temperate heat of the mine, it is converted into the nature of that same earth, which undergoes fixation* etc. To which the most learned Belgian, *Ewaldus Vogelius*, in his Commentary on Geber and *Ramon Llull*, comments thus: *Therefore Art, following Nature, does not receive quicksilver alone, nor sulfur alone, nor even silver...*

*quicksilver <note>original: "argentum vivum"</note> and sulfur together, but rather the same material mixed together and composed of the same principles, which nature has prepared for art. Petrus de Zalento calls this **Brumazar** <note>An alchemical term for a specific "elevated" state of matter</note>, namely an elevated mercurial-sulfurous vapor from a mercurial-sulfurous earth. The process—which Barnaudus cites in the *Theatrical Chemistry* <note>original: "Theatrum Chymicum," a massive compendium of alchemical texts</note> part 3, page 755—teaches how to reduce metals (even Gold itself) into this earth, and then to convert this earth into a mercurial Vapor, and to refreeze and fix it in its own earth. Take two ounces of pure gold <note>original: "Auri obrizi"</note>, mix it with ten times the amount of Mercury elaborated with great artistic skill, and dissolve it with a slow heat <note>original: "Vulcano," referring to Vulcan, the god of fire</note> until the mercury evaporates and the weight of the gold remains, reduced to a black powder. From this powder, draw out mercury using the heat of a water-bath until the powder turns into a snow-white lime <term>calx: the powdery metallic oxide formed after heating a metal</term>. Sprinkle this seven times with the water which was drawn from it by evaporation, and work with all care so that by this frequent impulse and shaking the substances refine themselves and emerge most pure from all filth and dregs. But a woman does not conceive at just any time, but only then when the womb has been prepared by nature for conception; therefore, take the purified lime—the **Sun of the Philosophers**—and in a sealed vessel, let it rot <note>original: "putrefac," the alchemical stage of putrefaction</note> for 40 days, until it melts into a thick white liquid. Into this, pour water gradually at proper intervals of days; this is the joining of the male and female, who are united in a marvelous way, and the female is entirely melted by the love of the male. This is the "solution." Leave it until it recovers its strength again, then let them join again, and do this as many times as necessary until the lime has soaked up all its water. Then let the "womb" be closed tight so that nothing escapes, for from that frequent thickening and dissolving the stone grows together. All the Philosophers explain which colors will appear; this powder proves these things to be true, for if a twelfth part of one grain of it is cast upon mercury, it will yield one drachm of gold (meaning one part transforms 720 parts). If you perform the multiplication, you will have no need of the stone, though this Process should suffice for you, as nothing is lacking. Farewell, and you are unhappy if you are turned away from this.*

THE SEVENTH and last species of artificial Ore is mine; and indeed I call it mine by right, since in this century I can state without boasting that I was either the first to find it, or the first to reveal it to the world once found. Certainly, I did so with no less disgrace, loss, labor, and time than **Christopher Columbus** discovered the New World. When he proposed his intent to the Royal Courts for a whole decade, he was everywhere regarded as a man out of his mind; yet when the proposal was finally put into effect, every scoundrel hurried to America, and it became more necessary to stop people from going there than it had been difficult to push them there the first time. What they think of me and my *perpetual Ore* in **Holland** is known in every barbershop, tavern, wagon, and ship, and in every gathering; meanwhile, however, while some publicly despise me and my Art as slanderers, others secretly lie in wait like deceivers and thieves. If, as was to be feared, this Art became publicly known, you would already count more Alchemists in Holland than almost Merchants. The "cursed hunger for Gold" <note>original: "Auri sacra fames," a famous quote from Virgil’s Aeneid</note> has driven some to such a point that, having seen even the smallest truth and possibility, they have sold their "cloak and boots" <note>original: "togam & caligas," a proverbial expression for all one's possessions</note> and spent it on this art. They would have progressed more happily and solidly if they had acted faithfully with me as the Author. But the common people want to be deceived; and what shall I say of the dregs of the People? I could produce the original authentic contracts and obligations for several thousands from certain locals and foreigners, who nevertheless...

## Becher’s Perpetual Martial Sandy Ore.

->The construction of this Ore consists of three parts.<-

**I.** In the copious extraction of Golden Sulfur from less precious bodies.
**II.** In the metallization, or incorporation of that Sulfur into Mercury (**Metallic**).
**III.** In the Bodification, Exaltation, fixation, and fusion of both.

### I.

### From which subjects the Golden tinging Sulfur can be copiously extracted, and by what Method one must proceed in its Extraction.

The goal of Alchemists is **to have Gold**; this can be obtained in only two ways, excluding the **Universal** <note>The "Universal" refers to the legendary Philosopher's Stone, capable of transmuting any substance.</note>. First, by extracting **Gold** from things in which it is realistically present in bodily form. This operation, however, is more metallic than **Alchemical**, although the **Alchemical Art** can contribute much to extracting, fixing, and liquefying bodies in which gold lies hidden—namely, so that **more than usual** may be acquired from it; hence it is called the **Art of Smelting** <note>original: "Ars Fusoria"</note>. Secondly, however, the genuine **Alchemical Art** consists partly, besides the Universal, in this: that it produces Gold from bodies from which nothing can be elicited by common means or the art of smelting. Therefore, Alchemy is distinguished: insofar as it pertains to the Universal, it is called **Tincturing**; but when it regards the preceding method of extracting Gold, it is called **Spagyric** <note>A term coined by Paracelsus, meaning to separate and to recombine.</note>, or the artificial **Philosophical** work of separation. ...accordingly <note>original: "fale", likely a continuation of "accordingly" from the previous page</note>, I set aside the tinctorial work <note>The "work of the tincture" refers to the process of turning base metals into gold via a catalyst.</note> for this time, and I shall deal solely with the **Separatory Work**: The foundation of which consists in this: Even if Gold appears to be a *homogeneous* body <note>meaning a uniform substance that cannot be broken down</note>, it is nevertheless composed of parts; specifically, as is commonly thought, of *Sulfur and Mercury*, as can also be proven. These parts, before they are combined gradually, are not Gold, and therefore are not worth as much as Gold is worth—much less should they be sold for it—but for a much lower price than when they have become perfected Gold after their conjunction. Therefore, the **Utility of Alchemy** consists in this: that the particles composing gold are found separately in "Subjects" <note>The raw materials or base substances used in an experiment.</note>, not yet joined into the form of Gold, which subjects cost very little; from these, by the help of the Art of Alchemy, they are extracted, joined, and thus reduced into Actual Gold, which is worth much. In this, therefore, properly consists the *Utility of Alchemy* regarding this part. What these low-priced species are, in which the seed of Gold lies hidden and joined, is necessary for the Alchemist to know above all else, for these are the very Subjects of his Art in which he must work; for when he is ignorant of these, all his expenses, sweat, and labors are in vain, and time is uselessly wasted. Therefore, although it has been discovered for many centuries that the seed of Gold is dispersed throughout the entire World in all Bodies—though remotely—(see my *First Supplement to Subterranean Physics*, Aristotle, Albertus Magnus, Gerhard Dorn <note>Gerhard Dorn (c. 1530–1584) was a philosopher and editor of Paracelsus's works.</note>, and many others, for since Gold consists of the four Elements, it must necessarily be in all things composed of elements, when they are highly rectified and fixed), nevertheless, a **nearer Matter** has been found, in which the seed of Gold, already specified, can be acquired with easier effort and greater profit: To be sure, I will not speak of *Talc, Emery, Hematite, Cadmia, Antimony*, and similar Stony and Mineral Bodies; but in the Metals themselves, namely in *Mars and Venus* <note>In alchemy, Mars represents Iron and Venus represents Copper.</note>, whence that old Proverb arose:

...sulfur of **Mars** <note>original: "Martis"; refers to Iron</note> and **Venus** <note>original: "Veneris"; refers to Copper</note> were so subtle and fixed, and the **Mercury** in **Mars** and **Venus** were likewise prepared without earthiness, these two would be physical **Gold**, and would be worth as much; nor could the Artist afterwards wring anything out of them except with great labor, and nevertheless without fruit. But now, since the **Balance of the Elements** and temperaments—indeed, the *Crasis* <note>A Greek-derived term referring to the specific "blending" or "constitution" of a mixture.</note> of the mixture—in these two bodies do not agree well, these two bodies are still separable and divisible. Therefore, they are in the Artist’s hand and power, who is able to *separate, purify, exalt, refine, and fix* the golden **Tincture** from them, and to reduce them again into fixed **Mercuries**, and to join the reduced parts with them, and thus he can manufacture from them a *perfect* mixture, namely, **Gold**. It is no different from the **Glassmaker**, who first extracts the **Salts**, purifies them, prepares the **Sand**, joins them, and then reduces them into glass; truly a "Subject" <note>The material or substance being operated upon.</note> which persists against all elements, fierce fires, and accidents even more *than Gold itself*. Therefore, how such a philosophical separation of the golden *Sulfur from Mars and Venus* is to be made—in which the true and noble **Spagyric Art** <note>The "Spagyric Art" is another name for alchemy, specifically focusing on the separation and recombination of natural components to create medicine or refined materials.</note> alone consists—is, before all things, necessary to know: namely, the Practice of this Work.

The curious and scrupulous Physicians of our age, namely **Otto Tackenius** <note>A 17th-century German chemist and physician famous for his theory that all substances are composed of two principles: acid and alkali.</note> and others, have found through diligent investigation that all bodies, including minerals, consist of **Acid and Alkali**—that is, of *acid and salt*—and if one part of these exceeds the *Crasis* <note>the balanced mixture</note> of the compound, they can be dissolved and altered again. Now, it is known that *Mars and Venus contain much acid* within themselves; therefore *Air, water*, and all other things in which **Alkalis** or *salts* are present easily attack them. From this, they are corrupted and contract rust as well as verdigris—and indeed they do so more quickly and more greatly if these bodies are *ground down and refined*.

From this, the Artist can easily gather what process must be established with these bodies: namely, **First**, it is necessary for him to *Refine* them; **Second**, to corrode them by means of Alkali or salt and lead them to a reaction; **Third**, to separate the most subtle part which is liberated by this corrosion or reaction; **Fourth**, to purify, refine, and *fix* that part, and reduce it into a **Mercurial Body**. It is from this foundation—although it has been unknown to many Physicians—that it has happened for many *centuries past* that there have been several hundred processes and Artists who have all sought, worked upon, and described "Particulars" <note>A "Particular" is an alchemical process that produces a small amount of gold or silver, rather than the "Universal" transformation of all matter.</note> from the **Saffron of Mars and Venus** <note>original: "Croco Martis & Veneris"; referring to the oxides or powders created by calcining iron and copper.</note>. And they did so indeed in different ways and methods, though from *one and the same* preceding *foundation* of Alkali and *Salt*. From this, some have calcined *Mars and Venus* with **Sulfur**, others with **Salt**; others have treated them with *reverberating fire*; others have corroded them with *distilled vinegar, salt water*, and others with different *strong waters* <note>original: "fortibus aquis"; usually refers to nitric acid or other mineral acids.</note>, and thus they produced the **Saffron of Mars and Venus**. All found *Proofs of Gold* from it, yet *one more than another*; namely, as the operation of one was better than the other. Nor among a thousand processes—by reason of *cementations or gradations* <note>"Cementation" is a dry process for refining metals by heating them with salts; "Gradation" is a process to increase the quality or color of a metal.</note>, if only they rest upon this *foundation*—will one be found in which there are not Martial, Venereal, and Sulfurous Salts, and similar things of that kind, in both the *dry and liquid paths*. These include *injection, flux, fusion, cementing powders, or graduating waters*. 

However, let the Reader know—for I wish to forewarn him faithfully—not to presume to put this work into Practice through liquid Solutions, *unless he knows the Nature of Mars and Venus most perfectly*...

...[which] is hermaphroditic <note>In alchemy, "hermaphroditic" refers to a substance that possesses dual qualities, often meaning it can react with or be dissolved by both acidic and alkaline substances, or in this context, both types of "waters."</note>, and therefore dissolves in **Strong Water** <note>original: "Aqua Forti"; nitric acid</note> and **Royal Water** <note>original: "Aqua Regis"; a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acid capable of dissolving gold</note>. The combustible earth, which adheres most strongly and abundantly to these subjects, is of the same nature and solution. For this reason, it is very difficult to separate it using solvents; for a common solvent is either of the nature of **Strong Water** or **Royal Water**. If some metallic subject is of such a nature that it dissolves in both, then it cannot be separated; therefore, the solution is in vain. You should, therefore, strive for such a solvent that is of a *mixed or neutral* nature. Next, the *Earth must be separated from the Sulfur* in the best possible way; for if that earth is left behind, the sulfur will always melt back into a metallic body or *Slag* <note>original: "Scoriam"; the stony waste matter separated from metals during smelting</note>. Then you may know for certain that your extraction is worth nothing. But if you have the true *Metallic Sulfur of Venus <note>Copper</note> and Mars <note>Iron</note>*, which can *no longer by itself* be reduced into a metallic body, then I tell you in truth that it *can tinge silver into gold*, or give to Gold itself an over-abundant, excellent, and fixed, perpetual color.

Only be concerned with the fixation of the Body; for here you have found a certain *kind of subtle Earth* which truly and *essentially* grows into Gold and Silver, and is inseparably woven into its atoms. Indeed, this Sulfur can be obtained from the substance itself, and Gold can reclaim from another what it had lost of its own; but that Sulfur from Venus <note>Copper</note> and Mars <note>Iron</note> is better. The things I write in this place are true; those who likewise know and have seen them can bear witness. Hence **Geber** <note>An influential 8th-century alchemist (often identified with the Latin writer pseudo-Geber) whose works laid the foundation for medieval chemistry.</note> rightly writes in the *Book of Furnaces*, chapter XVIII: *And let your aid be Venus best purified and dissolved, since from her is extracted the purest Sulfur, tinging and fixed.*

### II.

### On Metallization, or the induction of Golden Sulfur into Mercury.

It has always been thought that the first Matter of the World was *Water*, which not only the first chapter of Holy Scripture proves, but all philosophers, both Heathen and Christian, have asserted. In my own **Subterranean Physics** <note>original: "Physica Subterranea"; the most famous work of Johann Joachim Becher, published in 1669, which laid the groundwork for the phlogiston theory.</note> and its two supplements, I have also clearly demonstrated how all things arise, circulate, and are produced from *Water*, and by what reason a shining Fire exists within it, the subtlest part of which is transmuted into the stars, and the other part into Animals, Vegetables, and Metals. I rest in the hope that this opinion of mine is most likely true, because, as nothing better has been investigated thus far, it has been contradicted by no one. However, Water is not to be regarded as an Element or a simple body, as the Most Illustrious **Mr. Robert Boyle** <note>Robert Boyle (1627–1691) was a founding figure of modern chemistry, though he also practiced alchemy.</note> rightly teaches in his *Sceptical Chymist*, but it must be considered a mixed Being, which contains much of a certain Earth within itself that is of an earthy and false nature; as the universal *Sea*—the greatest part of the world—proves. This salt, if it is well examined, will be found to be endowed with a Sulfurous nature. Moreover, the species of Sulfurs are of diverse natures: *some burn and shine* and are combustible; some shine and are incombustible, just as the Sea itself, especially the Adriatic, or even *Human Urine* <note>original: "Hominis Urina"; urine was a common source of chemicals for early chemists, famously used by Hennig Brand to discover phosphorus around this time.</note> sufficiently shows. Similarly, Water also—or much more its false Substance, which is clothed in Sulfur—contains much...

...exists diversely; namely according to its purity, thinness, and sulfur. From this also the three great fluidities arise, which are clearly distinct: namely water, **Oil**, and **Quicksilver** <note>original: "Argenti vivi"; literally "living silver"</note>: these and no others are in the world. Regarding Mercury <note>original: "Mercurio"</note> therefore, to speak of that which I uniquely aim at—namely that wonderful water which does not wet the hands <note>A common historical description of liquid mercury, which behaves like a fluid but does not leave a residue on skin</note>, and about which all the Philosophers write—I have always maintained, and still maintain, that it *is a composite* consisting of much sulfur or fatness, and endowed with the greatest weight that any body in the world can enjoy. For God created volatile, heavy, fixed, transparent, shining, and opaque bodies, and these sometimes pure, sometimes mixed.

To come to **Quicksilver**, it is a heavy, liquid, penetrating, yet volatile substance, as is manifest. For it penetrates leather, weighs almost as much as gold, and yet is entirely volatile, so much so that it is held as a new paradox in philosophy: that a body should be heavy, penetrating, subtle, and volatile—and indeed so subtle that no spirit **of wine** <note>alcohol</note> can rival it. Just as this is assumed without contradiction and appears in the mines, in the **form of a vapor** it penetrates **Massive Stones** several hundred fathoms <note>original: "orgyjas"; an ancient unit of length roughly equal to the span of a man's arms</note> deep, and there generates metals. 

So it is certain that Quicksilver contains within itself a subtle, pure, and immutable **Sulphurous Spirit**, which can be destroyed by no element, as Experience in its anatomy <note>In this context, "anatomy" refers to the chemical analysis or breaking down of a substance</note> or analysis proves. Therefore, it must be considered a subject of *infinite wonder*, as many philosophers write. For it is in truth the pure, unadulterated essence **of Sea Salt**, namely a sulphurous salt, entirely analogous to the **Sulfur of common salt**, from which it also drew its origin: namely, through the distillation of **sea salt** into the caverns of the Earth (as I have demonstrated more extensively in my *Subterranean Physics* <note>original: "Physica Subterranea"; a seminal work by Johann Joachim Becher published in 1669</note>) and there, through sublimation and the mixing of a certain **subtle Earth**, it acquired its opacity; yet it can be reduced back to transparency, namely into a **transparent liquor**. 

For there is known to me a **transparent**, watery liquor, **equal in weight to Mercury**; whether it be that celebrated **Alkahest** <note>A hypothetical universal solvent sought by alchemists</note>, I will not define, but leave it to the reader to consider whether I have perfected this liquor by the *decomposition* of more transparent earth or **shining salt**, or by the *extraction* of opaque earth from Mercury. Certainly

"I know that Mercury is increased from common salt, and often, when increased, tends toward a transparent wateriness. He who knows how to separate Sulfur from Salt will be able to agree and believe me, that not only the brightness of Mercury, but also the splendor of **Pearls** is present in, owed to, and dedicated to this Sulfur.

I pass over the fact that, for greater confirmation, common salt produces several effects proper to Mercury, as much in medical and physical power as in alchemical. But how great a mass of salt is in one pound of Mercury can easily be guessed. It is better, therefore, to take this concentrated subject—which can be obtained at a cheap price, or even cheaper—into one's hands and consider its specific quality. This properly consists in the fact that it is highly separating, digesting, penetrating, inducing, and although it is itself volatile, it is nevertheless **fixing** <note>original: "figens"; the process of making a volatile substance stable or solid</note>. What it is worth in the human body is manifest; but to speak of metals, it cannot be denied that it amalgams itself with them, which cannot happen without solution and reaction. Perhaps, therefore, a **resolving** Sulphurous Salt must be present in it (for it [dissolves] gold through Mer- <note>The text cuts off here, continuing with the catchword "curium" on the next page to form "Mercurium" (Mercury)</note>

...[Mer]cury <note>original: "curium"; the first part of "Mercurium" is on the previous page</note> converted into salt, I have seen (without any other substance) that it can be further strengthened; from this, it earned its name among craftsmen, because I have called Mercury treated in this artificial manner sometimes *sharpened* and sometimes *animated* <note>In alchemy, "sharpening" usually refers to increasing the corrosive or reactive power of a solvent, while "animating" refers to giving "life" or metallic "soul" to quicksilver</note>. Therefore, the quality of Mercury cannot be better strengthened than by a mineral sulfurous Salt, which Nature has implanted in certain bodies that are already minerals. Two of these primarily hold the prerogative to which Quicksilver amalgams itself; by this reasoning, in its own Salt and its resolving quality, it is strengthened beyond all measure. Thus, once this kind of amalgamation is completed, it volatilizes Gold and *Silver* with itself, penetrates them, and makes them suitable for tinctures. 

To arrive at the Practice by degrees, let us first take an example: if ten parts of common Quicksilver are amalgamated with approximately one part of *lead* or *tin*, it will immediately—by its highly resolving quality—dissolve that metal just as ice dissolves in water. This could not happen unless it were equipped with the greatest resolving power. Once the metal is thus dissolved (understand that the *amalgam must be well rubbed and mixed*, then placed in a dish for gentle digestion), the Mercury, within the space of twelve hours, separates a *grey or black* earthy powder and ejects it to the surface. This powder should be removed to one side with a feather, and the digestion continued until such black powder ceases to appear. 

This is the sign that the Mercury has completed a perfect separation within the metal. For it must be well noted that all metals float upon Quicksilver, except for gold and silver; therefore, although other metals may be mixed with it through amalgamation, they are eventually raised up by it again, float on the surface, and undergo separation. That which remains when the Mercury is squeezed through leather <note>A common method for filtering liquid mercury from solid amalgams</note> is good and can be tested; but that which floats on top—namely the black powder—is the Sulfur or *soul of the metals* <note>original: "anima metallorum"</note>. When this is fixed and projected onto Silver, tested, and separated, it also yields upright Gold. Mercury itself is *sharpened, animated, and increased* by this very operation, and it becomes the *Mercury of Bodies* <note>A term for mercury that has been "philosophically" prepared to act upon other metallic bodies</note>. It also retains within itself the best part of the *tincture of the bodies*, and becomes better and better for the same operation if it is employed in such work again. 

For the Reader should know for certain that the purpose of this Discourse is this: unless Metallic or Mineral bodies, or Earths, or Stones, or extracts from them, enter into Mercury in some way and can be amalgamated with it, they will never produce a true and politically standing <note>Meaning "legally recognized" or "marketable" gold that passes the tests of the mint</note> increase with Gold. 

From this arose that famous deception of the "Increase of Gold" through the extract of *Spanish Emery* <note>original: "Smiridis Hispanici"; Emery is a rock used as an abrasive, here cited as a fraudulent additive</note>; this "increase" survives the processes of *Cupellation and Quartation* <term>Cupellation and Quartation are metallurgical assays used to separate precious metals from base metals and silver from gold</term>. However, if such gold is amalgamated with Mercury, it is again ejected and separated like a red earthy powder. 

*Learn therefore to purify and refine the earth for so long, until it pleases the Mercury, and is waxed by him <note>original: "inceretur"; to reach a waxy, fusible state in alchemy</note>, and he confirms it with his caduceus <note>The staff of Mercury, symbolizing the union of opposites</note> and grants it metallicity. Do not be weary if you suffer a rejection from him several times; prepare the rejected Earth better, and offer it to him again, and do this as many times as necessary until, taking pity on you, he accepts it.* 

Thus, that which seemed *gross, earthy, heterogeneous, styptic* <note>astringent or harsh</note>, and finally useless, will be *thinned, refined, waxed*, and perfected into the *best metal*. In this way, particular alterations and transmutations of Minerals, Metals, and their Sulfurs are achieved, and all by the Help of Mercury. 

How difficult it is, truly, to [yoke] Mars <note>Iron</note> to Mercury... <meta>The catchword "jungere" (to join/yoke) indicates the next page will discuss the difficulty of combining iron with mercury.</meta>

...to join, our Geber <note>Geber, or Jabir ibn Hayyan, is the legendary 8th-century father of Islamic alchemy whose works were central to European alchemical thought.</note> admits in the first part of the second Book, Chapter 65, when he writes: *And therefore [Mercury] does not adhere to Mars, except by the most subtle skill.* <note>original: "Ideoque non adhæret (sc. Mercurius) Marti, nisi subtilissimo ingenio." If those in Holland—who fled the school before their time without paying me the tuition, having only learned the preparation of a certain *special Saffron of Mars* <note>original: "Croci Martis"; iron oxide, typically used as a pigment or a stage in transmutation</note>—had waited long enough until they also learned its *inceration* <note>original: "incerationem"; the process of softening a dry substance to a wax-like consistency through the gradual addition of a liquid</note>, they would have acted more prudently. Therefore, let the curious reader thank me for this section and the *detected error* alone. For a long time, I observed the term TO CONFIRM in the books of the ancient chemists, but I always believed it was the same as *to fix*, until I later learned by experience that it is one thing *to be fixed*, and another *to be metallic* and *to have entry.*

### III.

### On the Corporification, Exaltation, Fixation, and Fusion of the Species of this Perpetual Mineral.

It is a very ancient opinion that metals consist of *Quicksilver* <note>original: "Argento vivo"; Mercury</note>, which is coagulated and fixed by a *terrestrial Sulfur*; and that according to the *degree* of purity and the quantity of *Quicksilver* and *Sulfur*, the metals are specified and diversified. Since this opinion has now been accepted by common use, it can easily be concluded that the alteration, transmutation, and perfection of metals consist in the maturation and purification of Mercury by means of a *Sulfurous substance* of a hot and astringent quality. I will not now deal with the Mercurial substance transmuted into a Sulfurous one and brought to the highest degree of purity, subtlety, and fixity—and so concentrated and refined that one part of it can constrain several thousand parts of raw quicksilver and transmute them into a fixed metal, which operation the Alchemists call a *Tincture* <note>The "Tincture" or Philosopher's Stone was believed to be a concentrated substance that could "dye" or transform base metals into gold.</note>. I will only demonstrate that the Acid of Sulfur can particularly alter and perfect the Alkali of the Mercury of metals. Truly, I would have to write an entire volume if I wished to recount all the *Species of Sulfurs* and all the ways of proceeding with them. I could set forth a thousand *Processes* from which it could be sufficiently demonstrated that the *Mercurial* substance of metals is altered, corrected, and perfected by *sulfurous acid*. But with these preliminary matters having been touched upon, it should be known that some have treated common Mercury with common Sulfur and have seen some effect from this supposition. Others, however, of a slightly deeper investigative nature, have directed their minds toward *Lead*, because on account of its weight and subtlety...

...they suspected that Mercury possessed a certain abundant subtlety; for its maturation and fixation <note>In alchemy, "maturation" is the ripening of a "base" metal into a "noble" one (like gold), and "fixation" is the process of making a volatile substance, like Mercury, withstand heat without evaporating.</note>, they were anxious for another **Sulfureous** agent. This they found nowhere more cheaply, abundantly, or quickly than in **Sand and Iron (otherwise known as Mars)**. For these reasons, having undertaken the work, they established various operations, the most important of which I will recount here—common ones, yet practicable on a large scale; the more subtle and more **Philosophical** ones he [the reader] will gather either from himself or from what has preceded.

Thus, some have melted **Lead with Iron** (employing, however, a prudent manipulation) and, having rejected the **Scoria** <note>Scoria: the dross or slag left over after smelting metal.</note>, they refined the **Saturn** <note>Saturn is the alchemical name for lead.</note> by cupellation, and repeated the labor. Others made **Glass** or **Enamel** <note>original: "Amauusum"; a lead-based glass often used to imitate gems.</note> in the usual way with **Saturn and Sand**, precipitated it with **Iron**, and reduced it back to metal, repeating this work several times until finally refining the **Lead**. The intention of all these men was to burn away and separate the **Sulfureous-earthy dross of the Lead**, and through this to purge, preserve, and wash the **Mercury of Saturn**, and to bind, heat, cook out, mature, and perfect it through the acid of the **Sand and Iron**. Nor did the result fail to respond to their prayer and effort. As an example of this, I will bring forward one or two raw and coarse experiments; and so that they may deserve better belief, although I have proven them myself, I will nonetheless attach the names of those men whom I have known and who are not unknown in the **World**.

### First is the Extract of one Operation performed in the Year 1657 in the Month of November at Amsterdam by the Assayer Grill, from his own Diary and Manuscript.

He took 950 lbs. of Lead and melted it upon a large ash-bed <term>ash-bed: "Cineritium," the porous material (often bone ash) used in a cupel to absorb oxidized base metals.</term> under a furnace vault; and while it was in motion, he added **Steel of iron** <note>original: "Stomoma ferri"; from the Greek "stomoma," meaning the hardened edge or essence of iron/steel.</note> successively from the beginning to the end of the **Cupellation**, 1 1/4 lbs. When all the Lead had been absorbed by the ash-bed, there remained a **Mass of silver** weighing 2 Marks and 1 1/4 ounces.

The **Ash-bed**, in which the Lead had been consumed, was crushed into pieces the size of walnuts, and 300 lbs. of copper slag, 100 lbs. of **Litharge** <note>Litharge: lead oxide, often a byproduct of silver refining.</note>, and 50 lbs. of **Tartar** <note>Tartar: potassium bitartrate, used here as a flux to help the metals melt and flow.</note> were added; all mixed together in a furnace prepared for this, they were vitrified [turned to glass], yielding a greenish **Glass and a Metallic Regulus** <note>Regulus: a lump of reduced, purified metal found at the bottom of the crucible.</note> weighing 117 1/2 lbs.

This **Glass was reduced** <note>"Reduced" here means the chemical process of turning an oxide or ore back into its metallic form.</note> over coals in a reduction furnace, giving seven metallic masses weighing 897 lbs., which were again cupelled and treated as before, with the addition of the prior Silver weighing 2 Marks and 1/4 ounce. Then, when the second operation was finished, the mass of Silver upon the ash-bed weighed 5 Marks of Silver minus a half-ounce; and each Mark held a **value of gold worth 35 stivers**. <note>original: "Stübers"; the stiver was a Dutch coin.</note>

Take 200 pounds of Lead, 10 Marks of Silver, and 20 pounds of Copper. Let them be refined in a cupel in the usual manner; during the refining, successively from start to finish, a spoonful of **steel of iron** is added, which is consumed within the space of a quarter hour. Having performed the refining...

### Practical Observations on the Aforementioned Process.

1. If, in the first refining, it pleases you to add a portion of **Tin** <note>original: "Jovis" or Jupiter, the alchemical name for tin.</note>, it can indeed be done, provided that no more than **half an ounce** is injected at one time, so that the glass-making (vitrification) of the Lead is not hindered. The injection of Tin in the manner described may be continued as desired, observing, as stated, that the vitrification is not blocked. However, care must be taken that no more than **one pound** of Tin is added to the **entire mass**, lest the material reduced from the Cupel be hindered by the Tin in further refining. Tin, moreover, should only be added in the first refining.
2. It would be better if the vitrification of the Cupel were done by **flame alone** rather than by the fire of coals, since coals tend to **reduce** <note>In chemistry, reduction is the process of turning a mineral or oxide back into a metal; here, it would prevent the lead from turning into glass.</note> rather than vitrify.
3. A Cupel made from **washed ashes** is better than one made from **bones**, because it vitrifies more easily.
4. Whatever weight is lost from the original mixture (which weighed 225 pounds) during each reduction should be replaced with new lead. After several operations and reductions—say three or four—a portion of **Copper** <note>original: "Veneris" or Venus.</note> and **Tin** can be added again.
5. If this operation is performed three or four times, an increase in **Silver** and **Gold** may be observed.

---

### Improvement of this Process according to my Observations.

1. IN PLACE of Copper and Iron <note>original: "Veneris, & Martis."</note>, their **Crocus** <term>Crocus: a fine powder, usually a metallic oxide, named for its saffron-like color.</term> could be used.
2. In the preparation of the Cupel, a portion of **mud**, **sand**, and **quicklime** could be added for greater "fixation" <note>Fixation refers to making a substance resistant to heat so it does not evaporate.</note> and easier vitrification.
3. In place of Saturn <note>Saturn is the alchemical name for Lead.</note>, it would be better to use the Lead of **Antimony** or the Lead of **Iron**.
4. **Marcasite** and **Bismuth**, as well as **fixed Sulfur**, **fixed Arsenic**, or **fixed Cinnabar**, would also be beneficial; extracts of **jasper**, **garnets**, **Emery**, **red ochre**, **hematite**, and other coloring species could also be added.
5. It would be better if the substances placed into the Lead were first melted separately with the Silver.
6. Tin <note>original: "Jupiter"</note> should be refined with **Niter** <note>Niter is saltpeter (potassium nitrate).</note>; in this way, it will enter the Lead without swelling, and a larger quantity of it can be added.

# Judgment on this Process.

The intention is for the dyeing species—specifically the sulfur of **Iron** <note>original: "Martis"; alchemists associated the planet Mars with iron.</note>—to enter the **Silver** <note>original: "lunam" or the Moon</note>, making it compact and colored. This results in the generation of **Gold** <note>original: "Solis" or the Sun</note>. Meanwhile, the combustible sulfur of **Copper** <note>original: "Veneris" or Venus</note> is absorbed through vitrification <note>The process of turning a substance into glass through intense heat.</note>, and the body of the Copper is whitened, which causes an increase of Silver in this process. The ashes of the **Cupel** <note>A porous vessel used in refining</note>, acting as a dry earthy body, absorb the combustible moisture of **Lead** <note>original: "Saturni" or Saturn</note>, Copper, and Silver. During reduction, the metallic bodies are rendered drier, especially since *a bit of the substance of the ashes essentially enters the metallic mixture*. It would be better, however, if the dyeing species could be "waxed" <note>An alchemical term meaning to soften a hard substance to a wax-like consistency so it can be combined with others.</note> so that they could enter the Silver without needing Lead; for Lead absorbs the better part of the dyeing agents. Yet vitrification, as the essential part of the other process, is necessary in every way here.

## A Second Experiment,
### Which proves that through the Destruction and Reduction of Metals they are thoroughly transmuted.

->IT IS<-

### By Doctor Tilenius, formerly a Physician of Frankfurt, which proceeds as follows.

Take half an ounce of **Lead** <note>original: "Saturni"</note>. When it begins to "flash" <note>The sudden brightening of the metal during cupellation.</note> in the cupelling crucible under a vaulted tile, add one drachm of **Tin** <note>original: "Jovis" or Jupiter</note> and several grains of **Silver** <note>original: "Lunae"</note>. Leave it for a while until it is entirely turned into **Scoria** <term>Scoria: the dross or slag left over after smelting metal</term>. If you melt this scoria in a stronger crucible, you will obtain a **Regulus** <term>Regulus: the pure metallic heart or "button" that settles at the bottom of a crucible</term> and a portion of the metals not yet reduced resting upon it; save this. From the Regulus, make scoria again under the tile as you did before, and examine the remaining metal in the Cupel. Grind this cupel together with the scoria leftover from the reduction (which I told you to save) and with the scoria produced by the cupelling crucible the second time. Reduce this powder again, adding any grain of Silver the cupel might have yielded. Turn the Regulus back into scoria once more, and proceed with the Regulus and scoria as before. If you repeat this labor several times—three or four—take the powder from the scoria and the cupel (which is now heavy with metals) and reduce it with 3 or 4 parts **Potash** <note>original: "Cinerum Clavellatorum"</note> in a strong crucible over a very fierce fire. You will then have pure grains of **Copper**.

## A third [experiment] I add, discovered by my own special experience.

**Cement** <note>Alchemical "cementation" involves heating a metal surrounded by powdered materials to purify it or change its properties.</note> and melt metals with **Mud** (or clay), **Bricks**, or **Sand**; reduce and treat them in this way several times. If you proceed well and repeat the work, you will find a useful perfection and transmutation of metals, even without the help of any **Tincture** <note>In alchemy, a "Tincture" is a potent substance capable of transforming base metals into gold or silver.</note>.

## The Fourth Experiment is found in the Third Part of Glauber’s Mineral Work in the following manner.

Metals can also be purified and washed—if they have first been reduced to a Lime <note>A powder produced by heating a metal, now known as an oxide.</note>—by means of sand or flints, and by the <term>glass of Lead</term> <note>original: "vitro Saturni"; a mixture of lead oxide and silica used as a flux in refining.</note> made therefrom, so that they yield a great deal of gold. However, a great deal of this glass of Lead is required for this labor, for the metal must be widely diffused and diluted within it if it is to set aside its dross and deposit its purer and heavier part. Sand or flints are used for this purpose so that they might attract the dross of the impure metals and separate the pure from the impure, just as if someone wished to purify honey, sugar, or another vegetable liquor with water and mixed in egg white, which attracts the impurity of the honey or sugar and purifies it. Thus, in this operation, the flints take the place of the egg white, and the **Lead** <note>original: "Saturnus"</note> performs the role of the water, by which the body of **Iron, Copper, or Tin** <note>original: "Martis, Veneris, vel Jovis"</note> is dissolved. This operation is very curious, easy, and swift, and a great profit could be made in a short time if vessels could be found that could withstand <term>litharge</term> <note>original: "lithargyrium"; lead oxide, which is highly corrosive to ceramic crucibles at high temperatures.</note> so that they were not perforated and the mixture lost. Provided the glass of Lead could withstand ten or twelve hours, then there would be no other way needed to become rich. Hitherto I have not been able to be so fortunate, although I have sought it for many years; however, I do not doubt that in the course of time someone will be found who is to discover it. One pound of **Iron, Copper, or Tin** occasionally yields a quarter, or even half an ounce of pure Gold, if you proceed correctly; and if you cast in some <term>fixed salt of Tartar</term> <note>original: "sal fixum Tartari"; potassium carbonate.</note> or even just <term>Potash</term> <note>original: "Cineres Clavellatos"; a caustic salt derived from wood ashes.</note>, you will receive even more, though the mixture also effervesces and runs over more easily, which is to be lamented. *Thus far Glauber; who repeats a similar labor in his "New Chemical Light," likewise in the first part of his "Mineral Work," and elsewhere.*

Regarding which, it should be noted that I had earthenware vessels made in Rotterdam which withstood the fire for twelve hours, in which I performed a great Trial at The Hague, which can still be seen, and which held the glass of Lead perfectly throughout that entire time, so that not even the smallest amount leaked out. Thus, the *Hollanders* truly do themselves an injury when they proclaim their Fatherland unsuitable for this Art. As far as this process is concerned, I have written an entire Commentary upon it with some hundreds of observations, but the same thing has happened to me as happens to almost all alchemists: they do not care for the present, they desire the future; and he who has once drunk wine would be a fool if he wished to labor at drawing water. Meanwhile, however, time and life are lost, and in my goal, which was unique, I have been most poorly deceived. Specifically, I wished to sell such operations—looking only toward *profit*—to merchants who gasp for profit alone, so that I might acquire a sum of money at one time, by which I could live quietly and finish my Philosophical labors. But as the said *Little Peasant* <note>original: "parvus Rusticus"; likely a reference to the alchemical author "Rusticus," a pseudonym for a supposedly simple but wise practitioner.</note> Philosopher complains, whenever he had it in his mind to perform the Great *Work*, the Devil hindered him everywhere, whether through friends, neighbors, or others; and how many years **Bernard of Trevisan** <note>A 15th-century alchemist famous for his long travels and eventual success in the art.</note> nested in various parts of the world until he found a corner suitable for hatching his golden egg, his book testifies. What will become of me, I myself still do not know. If I am expelled from Europe, shall I not betake myself to India? But concerning these things, more this coming summer. Now for

As a conclusion to this third Section, I add only this: that the entire foundation of the operation consists in the **Vitrification** <note>The process of turning a substance into glass through heat.</note> and **Reduction** of metals. In this way, their "earthiness" is successively drawn away, and the mercurial part is fixed and purified. For **Glass** is of such a nature that it allows entry to all things, preserves metals in a state of flow, and fixes volatile substances and mineral vapors; for this reason, the Ancients not unfairly called it the "Mud of Wisdom" and the ***Seal of Hermes***. It preserves bodies from the fire so they are not scorched, and it provides many useful things, especially in gold made by art—which is still "tender"—to which it gives fixation, exaltation, and permanence. Therefore, I say as a conclusion to this entire Seventh Mineral: *Seek your golden Sulfur in those subjects in which it is abundant and plentiful; refine it, purify it, and join it to the mercurial flow. Then, do not proceed with it immediately in the **Cupel**, but first fix and incorporate it with some good Glass; finally, commit it to the assay. But see that you are not deceived by **Aqua fortis**, as happened to me at **The Hague**, where the Aqua fortis—prepared from unrefined nitre containing much common salt—became more like **Aqua regia** than Aqua fortis. Thus, it dissolved the bodily Gold itself rather than separating it, as I later demonstrated to the eye by the precipitation of Mercury. He, therefore, who knows how to refine* without a cupel, *which is done through* Vitrification, *and how to separate* without aqua fortis, *which is done through* precipitation, *will work more profitably. And so much for the* common, coarse Seventh Mineral, *which you can nevertheless immediately convert into the* **Philosophical** *one, if in place of crude **Lead** you take its Mercury; if in place of crude **Iron** and **Copper** you take their Sulfur and soak the Mercury with it; and if in place of bodily glass, you "incerate" <note>To mix with wax or a waxy substance to soften it.</note> the precipitate with Oil of Glass. You will rejoice in these words and deeds.*

And so, by a studious and hardworking "Ariadne's thread," <note>A reference to the mythological thread used to escape the Labyrinth; here, it refers to a guiding logic through complex alchemical steps.</note> I have explained myself out of the depths of these **seven Minerals** by the grace of God, and have once again come forth from darkness into the light. This I have done against the will and expectation of all my enemies, whose persecution forced this disclosure of the Seven Minerals from me; yet I still know many secret, wealthy tunnels within, to be reserved for friends alone.

# Upon what Physical or Mineral foundation is this "Sandy Proposition," made to the Lords of the States, founded? Or does it find reason and place in Philosophy?

That minerals and metals, especially Gold and Silver, are mixed and composite terrestrial things is demonstrated both by their weight and other terrestrial qualities, as well as by touch and solidity. However, that they do not all share one "Earth" as their principle (according to their different species) is proved by their variety and the diversity of their color, solidity, ductility, and other qualities. Finally, it is also clear that any mineral or metal, considered not just in respect to others but in respect to itself, does not consist of one simple earth alone, but has come together into a certain mixture with several others...

It happens that the dissolution, **vitrification**, and reduction into **Mercury** and **vitriol** of such a mixture or metallic body proves this. These operations would not only vary across different metallic species, but would also produce different and successive effects within each individual species if all metallic species were formed from one single earth, or if any specific metallic species were cast from one simple earthy principle. More can be read on these matters in the author’s *Subterranean Physics* <note>original: *Physica subterranea*; the seminal work by Johann Joachim Becher, first published in 1669</note>, especially in its first supplement. I bring this forward only so that the reader may be preliminarily informed about the **Crasis** <note>original: *Crasi*; a term from ancient medicine referring to the unique "temperament" or blending of elements that gives a substance its specific properties</note> and mixture of metals, so they may understand what follows more clearly.

With these things assumed and established—namely, that **metals**, and among them even **Gold** and **Silver**, are mixed and composed of different earths, as reason and experience easily demonstrate—we then conclude by infallible and consequent reasoning: those earths or terrestrial principles entering the mixture of **Gold** and **Silver** and composing that metal are by no means an absolute metal separately before they meet or actually unite in that mixture (that is, before they effectively constitute a metal). Therefore, in such a state—namely, before their conjunction and mixing—they cannot be worth as much in market value as after conjunction, when they have actually come together into the perfect **Crasis** of **Gold** and **Silver**. Just as the wheels of a clock are worth far less separately than when joined together, constituting a perfect **Automaton** <note>A self-moving machine; here used to describe the complex "mechanism" of a finished metal</note>; thus, he who knows how to find, purify, and join such primordial and separate mineral earths in the proper proportion will necessarily produce a metal effectively and actually, worth more than the principles cost before their conjunction.

At this point, I could point out certain earths of very little value found in various places and in great quantities, which their entry into and inseparable adhesion in such metals demonstrate to be the principles of **Gold** and **Silver**. Because of this, certain frauds are committed among deceivers and wicked men who know how to augment **Gold** and **Silver** through such earths; however, they usually induce brittleness because they are ignorant of the other required earths and the perfect mixture. To place one example before the reader’s eyes: common mud contains within itself a certain seminal metallic Earth. If this mud is mixed with its counterpart—namely, a **Mercurial** substance hidden in any fat or oil—it yields effective iron and, actually, **Gold** of good quality. See my first supplement to *Subterranean Physics*.

I presented this experiment to the entire world many years ago. Just as it is invincible, so much less should sand, gravel, grit, flint, and stones be called into doubt; for it is established by daily experience and is publicly visible that metals are generated and dug out in mountains, in rocks, and in stones. What else is a grain of sand compared to a hundred-weight rock, except that it differs in discrete and continuous quantity? Otherwise, a grain of sand is as much a stone as an entire mountain, which is seen through microscopes—namely, that individual grains of sand are transparent flints. Hence it is no wonder if daily experience finds various metals, especially a significant portion of gold, in sand in various places; such as in the **Rhine**, **Danube**, and **Tagus** rivers in **Spain**, in the **Mina** in **Guinea**, etc. Although someone might object that gold is not generated in such sand but is washed there from the underground **gold-bearing veins** <note>original: *venis auriferis*</note> of mountains, the contrary is clear...

Indeed, it is more capable of this than massive rocks due to its disjointed continuity, as massive stones are not so easily penetrated by mineral vapors. That flint and sand are of such a fixative nature and possess the faculty for receiving and retaining such vapors is demonstrated not only by eyewitness observation in the mines themselves, but also by experience outside the mines (see the first Supplement). *The vapor of common **Mercury** is most conveniently precipitated and fixed through flints or sand, which is why some have labored upon artificial ores with success*. From the aforesaid, it is therefore concluded:

*First*, Metals, even Gold and Silver, are bodies and earthy mixtures.

*Second*, they are ordinarily generated in stones, especially **Flints**.

*Third*, the stony substance is the matrix of metals, and some part of it passes into the metallic mixture.

*Fourth*, all semi-transparent sand and tiny flints are of the same substance; hence they are to be held as a metallic principle and as the matrix of metals.

From the aforementioned conclusions, the Author does not see by what reasoning this article could be opposed here in **Holland**, since it is founded upon an invincible argument: for either metals are not generated in stones (which is contrary to evidence), or stones contribute to the generation...

## SECTION G.
## Whether the Author’s Proposition also holds true for Dutch Sand?

Whether Gold is generated in Rock or in sand, and whether sand is diminished Rock, matters little to Dutch Merchants, who would much rather scrounge for gold than philosophize about it. Nevertheless, they are forced to believe that gold is found in the sand on the African coast in the region of Guinea, specifically in the River de Mino <note>likely the Elmina or "River of the Mine" in modern-day Ghana</note>, because they see such gold with their own eyes and possess it, carried home in their purses. But they deny with "full cheeks" <note>an idiom meaning to deny something loudly or vehemently</note>, and cry out until they are hoarse, that Dutch sand—whether from the shore or the hills—can provide the same. They are led to this denial by what they consider three "pregnant" or weighty reasons:

The *First* is that, far and wide, both within and around Holland, no minerals are found, nor even any traces of them. The *Second* is that neither by washing nor by amalgamation <note>the process of extracting gold by mixing it with mercury</note> can even the smallest amount or trace of gold be elicited from Dutch sand. The *Third* is that sand in hot places (since heat is otherwise necessary for the generation of metals) is of a better quality than in cold places, as proven by *experience*.

To these individual objections, I respond briefly. Indeed, to the *First*, I constantly contradict them, relying on *experience*: I deny that the mud and sand in Holland are non-mineral, since most of their peat-turves <note>original: *caespites*; blocks of peat burned for fuel</note> show evidence of metal and, if burned, demonstrate the presence of Arsenic. Not far from the city of *Haarlem* <note>original: *Harlem*</note>, a red arsenical earth is found which burns all crops, and is designated by the inhabitants with its own name. Near Haarlem, a mine of *Cobalt* <note>original: *Cobolti*</note> is also found, from which *Smalt* <note>original: *Smalta*; a blue pigment made from cobalt glass</note>, or a blue color, is prepared; there is also an *anonymous metal* which is neither Gold nor Silver, and yet resists the *Cupel* <note>original: *Cupella*; a small, porous vessel used in assaying to separate precious metals from base metals by heating</note> and *Strong Water* <note>original: *Aqua forti*; nitric acid, used by alchemists to test or separate gold from other metals</note>. The sand of *Overijssel* <note>original: *Transinsulana*; the Dutch province "across the IJssel"</note> contains some silver, and the red sand near *Arnhem* <note>original: *Arnhemium*</note> and *Silver-stone* <note>original: *Sulver-stein*</note> is gold-bearing, with a hundredweight of it containing one gold coin's worth. Therefore, things that are still uncertain and not sufficiently explored ought not to be denied as certainties. Let the Dutch not do an injustice to their own land, nor accuse it of a lack of those things which it provides so generously; rather, let them investigate its nature, and let them not envy others from abroad for what they themselves cannot find.

To the *Second Objection*—namely, that there is no potential gold in Dutch sand because none can actually be elicited from it by washing or amalgamation—I deny this entirely as a most false Objection. For I hear that a certain artisan was recently found who washes more Gold from sand than others; indeed, he does so from the very sand from which others could elicit nothing. Perhaps that art is not unknown to those who wash Gold in the Hungarian mines and wash-works upon cloths, and who deceive the Emperor of many thousands of *bits or grains of gold* <note>original: *bisestis seu granis auri*</note>. There is also a species of stones...

Therefore, it follows necessarily that something **potential** lies hidden in the sand, or a certain **form** of Gold, which acts upon the mercurial substance of lead or silver as a metallic matter, and perfects it into gold. Whether you say this power hidden in the sand is merely a **separating** faculty in lead and silver, or whether you call it **digestive, or fixing, or tinting, and graduating**, it matters little to me, provided it remains certain and firm that without the help of sand, no gold can be produced from it. Whether the sand concurs **formally, or instrumentally, or essentially, or accidentally** <note>These are Aristotelian categories of causation: the 'form' or essence, the 'instrument' or tool, the 'essential' nature, or the 'accidental' secondary property</note> toward this production of gold moves me little, as I have said; it is enough for me that it concurs, and in concurring it becomes a necessity—that is, a thing without which nothing happens. 

However, to satisfy the curious Reader more than the common people (who may be content with the aforementioned evidence), I will demonstrate the **existing power** of gold in the sand with brief but profound reasons grounded in Physics. It is an old opinion, known even to "the bleary-eyed and the barbers" <note>original: "lippis & tonsoribus nota," a Latin idiom meaning a fact so well-known that everyone, even those in a barber shop, gossips about it</note>, that all things consist of form and matter—namely, **Object** and **Subject**, like male and female. **Albertus** <note>Albertus Magnus (c. 1200–1280), a medieval scholar who wrote extensively on alchemy and nature</note> brought forth the innate heat and radical moisture; **Paracelsus** <note>The famous 16th-century Swiss physician who revolutionized chemistry</note> brought forth Sulfur and Mercury. The modern **Spagyricists** <term>Spagyrici: Alchemists who believed in "separating and recombining" substances to find their essence</term>, led by the observation of reactions, brought forth **Acid and Alkali** into the discussion, because they have seen through experience that no physical motion occurs, nor does any reaction happen, nor is any perfect mixture given, except through the mediation of acid and alkali. 

Thus, when the acid of **Salt** absorbs the Alkali of **urine**, then a certain mixture is made which they call **Sal Armeniac** <term>Sal Armeniacum: Now known as Ammonium Chloride; used in soldering and as a medicine</term>; but if the acid of common salt absorbs the Alkali of **Mercury**, then a mixture is made which they call **Sublimatum** <term>Sublimatum: Corrosive sublimate or Mercuric Chloride</term>; if the acid of tallow or oil absorbs a lye alkali, a mixture is given which they call **Smegma** <note>An old term for soap</note>; but if the acid of sand and the alkali of ashes react, then a mixture comes forth which they call **glass**, the **most indissoluble mixture of all mixtures**. 

So, if sand is mixed with **Lead**, as soon as it feels heat, the acid of the sand will work upon the Alkali of lead with a great reaction, fermentation, and swelling. Finally, when the reaction is finished, the effervescence calmed, and the mixture brought to the right temperament, a certain transparent mixture comes to light, like a hyacinth, which they call **Glass of Saturn** <note>Saturn is the alchemical name for Lead; Glass of Saturn is lead glass, valued for its clarity and weight</note>. From these reactions, it is manifest that the reacting power exists in its acid, which can also be tested by simple manual practice <term>Enchyrisi: a Greek-derived term for a hands-on chemical operation</term>; if **flints or sand are distilled by themselves** in a retort with a very strong fire, they will yield an acid liquor, a medicine for all malignant fevers that is incomparable and priceless—so much so that it was circulated by a certain great Practitioner under the name of **Potable Gold** <note>original: "Auri potabilis," a legendary alchemical elixir made of gold that was said to cure all diseases</note> with great applause through much of the world. 

Furthermore, those who make **Strong Waters** and **Gradatory Waters** <note>Nitric acid and other acids used to separate and refine metals</note> usually add flints or sand; and they think this happens because of "interposition" <note>acting as a physical spacer to prevent clumping</note>, so that the remaining materials do not flow together. But they err; for it does not happen because of this, but because there is a **graduating and fixing** power within the Flints. I knew a peasant living in the mountains who distilled a green water from a certain species of flint, by whose help...

There, immediately following the custom of that curious nation, my proposition was utterly rejected by some, heard by others, and taken into consideration by a few. This Secret might have spread so widely that even shoemakers, tailors, and potters—as some of them have already begun—would have devoted their efforts to Alchemy, and would have verified the prophecy which came forth nearly two centuries ago regarding this Year 1680: *namely, that at that time Alchemy would be in such common use that it would be taken up by craftsmen and peasants.* This, as I have said, would infallibly happen if such investigators first thought about and looked back to the principles—the causes of things and the reasons for their effects—before they hurried toward the end, as if toward some mere trade, like common laborers. For it is not enough to draw out Gold by the help of sand and metals, nor is it sufficient to know that this "gold-ness" is caused by the acid of the sand. 2. Although no actual Gold can be elicited from sand by the common method of washing and Amalgamation, nonetheless, as long as it is vitrifiable, it contains potential gold.

4. As often as Sand and lead alone, or with other Metals, are vitrified and reduced, so often are they perfected and improved.
